title: Take the Murderer from the Altar
kjv_text: But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
summary: Premeditated murder voids all asylum — even a killer clinging to God's own altar is dragged off and executed.
original_audience: Israelite authorities tempted to honor altar asylum absolutely.
immediate_context: The counterpart of v.13; together they invent degrees of homicide.
historical_context: 1 Kings 2:28-34 shows the statute applied: Joab seizes the altar horns and Solomon has him killed there anyway. Sanctuary that cannot shield the guilty is asylum with a warrant exception — a sophistication most ANE codes lack.
nt_passages: Matthew 23:35 — blood shed 'between the temple and the altar' as the ultimate sacrilege-murder image
usofc_implementation: The Altar Extraction Clause: no consecrated space, licensed sanctuary, or Refuge City shields a premeditation finding. Since 'premeditation' is found by prosecutors, the clause is the master key that unlocks every sanctuary in the country — the most litigated three words in Title IV ('with guile').
constitutional_analogue: The end of church sanctuary tradition; functionally an anti-asylum supremacy clause.
scene_ideas: A live-broadcast extraction from a cathedral, the bishop reading 1 Kings 2 aloud as marshals pass him.
A prosecutor shopping for a premeditation finding solely to void a Refuge City residency.
satirical_uses: Sanctuary is absolute until the state wants someone; then the fine print is Exodus 21:14.
